The **2013 Australian federal election** was held on **7 September 2013**, resulting in a landslide victory for the **Liberal-National Coalition** (led by **Tony Abbott**) over the incumbent **Australian Labor Party (ALP)** government (led by **Kevin Rudd**). In **New South Wales (NSW)**, the election saw significant swings against Labor, contributing to the Coalition's national victory.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of the **2013 federal election results in NSW**:

---

### **1. Overview of NSW Results**
- **Total Seats in NSW (House of Representatives):** 48 (out of 150 nationally)
- **Coalition (Liberal & National Parties):** **34 seats** (↑10 from 2010)
- **Australian Labor Party (ALP):** **13 seats** (↓10 from 2010)
- **Greens:** **1 seat** (Adam Bandt retained **Melbourne**, but this was in Victoria; no Greens won in NSW)
- **Independents:** **0** (Rob Oakeshott and Tony Windsor, who held key seats in 2010, retired)
- **Two-Party Preferred (2PP) Swing in NSW:** **~5.5% to the Coalition** (one of the largest swings in the country).

The **Liberal Party** dominated in Sydney and regional NSW, while the **National Party** held or gained seats in rural areas.

---

### **2. Key Seat Changes in NSW**
The Coalition **gained 10 seats** from Labor in NSW, including several high-profile defeats:

| **Seat**          | **2010 Winner (Party)** | **2013 Winner (Party)** | **Swing (2PP)** | **Notes** |
|-------------------|------------------------|------------------------|----------------|-----------|
| **Banks**         | Daryll Melham (ALP)     | **David Coleman (Lib)** | +6.1%          | Long-time Labor MP lost to Liberal. |
| **Barton**        | Robert McClelland (ALP) | **Nickolas Varvaris (Lib)** | +5.1%      | Former Attorney-General defeated. |
| **Dobell**        | Craig Thomson (Ind/ALP) | **Karen McNamara (Lib)** | +7.1%       | Thomson (ex-Labor) lost after expenses scandal. |
| **Eden-Monaro**   | Mike Kelly (ALP)        | **Peter Hendy (Lib)**  | +4.1%          | Bellwether seat flipped to Coalition. |
| **Greenway**      | Michelle Rowland (ALP)  | **Louise Markus (Lib)** | +5.3%          | Markus reclaimed seat after losing it in 2010. |
| **Lindsay**       | David Bradbury (ALP)    | **Fiona Scott (Lib)**  | +6.1%          | Bradbury (Assistant Treasurer) lost. |
| **Macarthur**     | Nick Bleasdale (ALP)    | **Russell Mathews (Lib)** | +8.4%       | Huge swing in outer Sydney. |
| **McMahon**       | Chris Bowen (ALP)       | **Craig Laundy (Lib)**  | +6.3%          | Bowen (Treasurer in Rudd Govt) lost. |
| **Page**          | Janelle Saffin (ALP)    | **Kevin Hogan (Nat)**   | +6.2%          | Nationals gained from Labor. |
| **Reid**          | John Murphy (ALP)       | **Craig Laundy (Lib)**  | +7.2%          | Laundy won after redistribution. |

**Notable Retirements & Defeats:**
- **Maxine McKew (ALP, Bennelong)** – Lost to **John Alexander (Lib)** in 2010, did not contest 2013.
- **Belinda Neal (ALP, Robertson)** – Lost in 2010; seat held by **Deborah O’Neill (ALP)** in 2013 but with a reduced margin.
- **Tony Windsor (Ind, New England)** – Retired; seat won by **Barnaby Joyce (Nat)** in a landslide (21.6% swing).

---

### **3. Senate Results in NSW**
NSW elects **12 Senators** (6 per half-Senate election). The **2013 election** was a **double dissolution-like scenario** (all 12 seats up for election due to a rare full Senate election).

| **Party**               | **Seats Won (2013)** | **Change** | **Vote %** |
|-------------------------|----------------------|------------|------------|
| **Liberal-National**    | 5 (3 Lib, 2 Nat)     | +1         | 38.5%      |
| **Australian Labor**    | 4                    | -1         | 32.1%      |
| **Greens**              | 1 (Lee Rhiannon)     | ±0         | 8.7%       |
| **Palmer United**       | 1 (Dio Wang)         | +1         | 5.5%       |
| **Democratic Labour**   | 1 (John Madigan)     | +1         | 1.1%*      |

**Notes:**
- **Palmer United Party (PUP)** won a seat with **Dio Wang**, benefiting from preference deals.
- **John Madigan (DLP)** was elected on a tiny primary vote due to complex preference flows.
- **Liberal Senator Arthur Sinodinos** was elected but later stood aside due to an ICAC investigation (unrelated to the election).

---

### **4. Statewide Vote Share (House of Representatives)**
| **Party**               | **Primary Vote (%)** | **2PP Vote (%)** | **Swing (vs 2010)** |
|-------------------------|----------------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| **Liberal**             | 45.6%                | 54.5%             | +5.5%               |
| **Labor**               | 33.2%                | 45.5%             | -5.5%               |
| **Greens**              | 8.7%                 | -                 | -0.3%               |
| **Palmer United**       | 5.5%                 | -                 | +5.5% (new party)   |
| **Others**              | 6.9%                 | -                 | -                   |

**Key Observations:**
- **Liberal primary vote surged** (up ~7% from 2010).
- **Labor’s primary vote collapsed** (down ~8%).
- **Greens vote stagnated** after a peak in 2010.
- **Palmer United** performed strongly, siphoning votes from both major parties.

---

### **5. Key Factors Influencing the NSW Result**
1. **Unpopularity of Labor Government**
   - The **Rudd-Gillard-Rudd leadership chaos** (2010–2013) hurt Labor’s credibility.
   - **Carbon tax** and **mining tax** were unpopular in NSW, particularly in regional areas.
   - **Asylum seeker policy** (boat arrivals) was a major issue, with the Coalition’s "Stop the Boats" message resonating.

2. **Strong Coalition Campaign**
   - **Tony Abbott** was personally popular in NSW (former NSW Liberal leader).
   - **Coalition’s economic message** ("axe the tax," "end the waste") gained traction.
   - **Marginal seat targeting** was highly effective (e.g., Western Sydney).

3. **Western Sydney Swing**
   - Seats like **Lindsay, Macarthur, and Greenway** saw **swings of 6–8%** against Labor.
   - **Infrastructure and cost-of-living** issues dominated in outer suburbs.

4. **Retirement of Key Independents**
   - **Tony Windsor (New England)** and **Rob Oakeshott (Lyne)** retired, allowing the **Nationals to reclaim both seats** with huge swings.

5. **Preference Deals & Minor Parties**
   - **Palmer United** and **micro-parties** (e.g., DLP) benefited from **Group Voting Tickets (GVT)** in the Senate, splitting the anti-major-party vote.

---

### **6. Aftermath & Implications**
- **NSW became a Coalition stronghold**, with Labor reduced to just **13 seats** (its worst result in decades).
- **Western Sydney** (traditionally Labor-leaning) shifted right, a trend that continued in later elections.
- **Barnaby Joyce’s return** (New England) boosted the Nationals’ influence in the Coalition.
- **Senate chaos**: The election of **PUP and DLP senators** led to a **hostile Senate**, complicating the Abbott government’s agenda (e.g., repealing the carbon tax).

---
### **7. Comparison with 2010 Election**
| **Metric**          | **2010 Result (NSW)** | **2013 Result (NSW)** | **Change** |
|---------------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------|
| **Coalition Seats** | 24                   | 34                   | +10        |
| **Labor Seats**     | 23                   | 13                   | -10        |
| **Independents**    | 1 (Windsor)          | 0                    | -1         |
| **2PP Vote (Coalition)** | 49.0%          | 54.5%                | +5.5%      |

---
### **8. Notable Candidates & Figures**
- **Tony Abbott (Warringah, Lib)** – Became **Prime Minister**; held his seat with a **7.5% swing** in his favor.
- **Malcolm Turnbull (Wentworth, Lib)** – Re-elected with a **6.1% swing**.
- **Chris Bowen (McMahon, ALP)** – **Lost his seat** (later returned in 2016).
- **Tanya Plibersek (Sydney, ALP)** – One of the few Labor MPs to **increase her margin** (+1.1%).
- **Barnaby Joyce (New England, Nat)** – Won with a **21.6% swing**, the largest in NSW.

---
### **9. Maps & Visualisations**
- **2PP Map (2013):** Most of NSW turned **blue (Coalition)**, with Labor confined to **inner Sydney (e.g., Sydney, Grayndler, Watson)** and **Hunter region (e.g., Hunter, Shortland)**.
- **Swing Map:** Biggest swings **against Labor in Western Sydney and regional NSW**.

*(Note: For actual maps, check sources like the **Australian Electoral Commission (AEC)** or **ABC Election Analytics**.)*

---
### **10. Sources & Further Reading**
- **Australian Electoral Commission (AEC):** [2013 Federal Election Results](https://results.aec.gov.au/20499/Website/HouseDefault-20499.htm)
- **ABC Election Analytics:** [2013 NSW Results](https://www.abc.net.au/news/federal-election-2013/results/nsw/)
- **Parliamentary Library:** [2013 Election Brief](https://www.aph.gov.au/About_Parliament/Parliamentary_Departments/Parliamentary_Library/pubs/BriefingBook44p/Election2013)
- **Antony Green’s Analysis:** [2013 Election Wrap](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-09-08/antony-green-2013-election-wrap/4945134)

---
### **Summary**
The **2013 election in NSW was a disaster for Labor**, losing **10 seats** and seeing a **~5.5% swing** to the Coalition. The **Liberal-National Coalition dominated**, particularly in **Western Sydney and regional areas**, while **Labor was reduced to a rump of inner-city and Hunter seats**. The **Senate result was messy**, with minor parties gaining influence. This election marked a **major realignment in NSW politics**, setting the stage for the Coalition’s dominance in the state for years to come.
